newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan says Libya visit was "victory".
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan says Libya visit was "victory".

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Wednesday defended a controversial trip to Libya condemned at home and abroad, as a victory for his Islamist diplomatic efforts.
"We have returned like victorious Roman commanders," Anatolian news agency quoted Erbakan as telling a news conference at Ankara airport on his return from a three-nation Africa tour.
The trip was marred by an controversial meeting with Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi last weekend.
Turkey's close ally Washington has severly criticised Erbakan for defending Gaddafi against U.S. charges of support for terrorism against the West.
But Gaddafi snubbed his host with an outburst against Turkey's Western leanings and treatment of its Kurds.
Erbakan said he had later explained to Gaddafi Turkey's need to combat separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels regarded by Ankara as terrorists.

"We made it very clear that no one has the right to support terrorism," Erbakan said. He played down a call from Gaddafi for the foundation of a Kurdish state, presumably on Turkish soil. "Gaddafi is known for making philosophical speeches like that."
Erbakan also visited Egypt and Nigeria, another state shunned by the West.
He repeated previous accusations that Washington aided the PKK by allowing Kurdish television station MED TV to hire satellite time from a company in the United States.
"I am asking you all, does friend and ally the United States not let MED TV make biased propaganda to the whole world every day?" he said.
He also charged that Britain, Belgium, France, Russia and the European Parliament backed the rebels, fighting for self-rule in southeast Turkey.
